svg.title: How Command Center graph workflows execute
svg.desc: A technical infographic showing a directed acyclic graph of execution contexts mapped onto reusable lanes. Each worktree lane owns one branch and worktree. At fan-out, one child reuses the parent lane while siblings fork from its committed head. At fan-in, Smart Merge converges source lanes before the downstream context runs. Once all work settles, final publish merges terminal lanes into the session worktree, and a separate gated merge delivers the session branch to the project target.

g.text: A context DAG becomes isolated execution lanes, converges at joins, publishes to the session, then crosses a gated delivery boundary.
Authored context = ordered tasks + acceptance criteria.
Ready contexts are placed onto reusable lanes
An advisory lane plan suggests reuse; runtime assigns or forks lanes as contexts become schedulable.
Fork starts at A's committed HEAD.
One child inherits the parent lane.
One lane maps to one branch + worktree.
TARGET: latest updatedAt · lane ID ↑ on tie
One context runs per lane; separate worktree lanes execute in parallel
branch csm/feature · unchanged in default worktree-lane mode
D starts after upstream output is recorded and visible on D's lane.
Pairwise Smart Merge auto-resolves conflicts and runs pre-merge validation; failure halts with saved progress.
does not mark the run Delivered.
EXAMPLE: FOUNDATION → {BACKEND, UI} → INTEGRATE · RUNTIME SOURCE: src/lib/workflow-graph · EDITABLE SVG
